candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p. 12 / PDF p. 16: apply knowledge of pharmacology when administering medications; identify indications/actions and monitor/evaluate medication therapy
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — antipsychotic pharmacology / aripiprazole receptor activity
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that aripiprazole has proposed partial agonist activity at dopamine D2 receptors rather than functioning as a pure full dopamine antagonist or agonist.

options.A: Partial agonist activity at dopamine D2 receptors
options.B: Irreversible blockade of all dopamine receptor subtypes
options.C: Pure dopamine agonist activity with no serotonergic receptor effects
options.D: No clinically relevant activity at dopamine receptors

candidate.rationale: DailyMed states that aripiprazole's mechanism of action is unknown, but its efficacy is proposed to be mediated through partial agonist activity at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT1A receptors together with antagonist activity at 5-HT2A receptors. Therefore A is correct. The other options contradict the labeled pharmacology.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Aripiprazole's efficacy is proposed to involve partial agonist activity at dopamine D2 receptors; the overall mechanism of action is not fully known.
candidate.source_locator: §12.1 Mechanism of Action: mechanism unknown; proposed efficacy mediated through partial agonist activity at D2 and 5-HT1A receptors and antagonist activity at 5-HT2A receptors
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
candidate.stem: Which receptor activity is part of the proposed mechanism contributing to aripiprazole's clinical efficacy?
